# Every topology commit re-derives ~330 lines of header presentation because header state has nowhere to live but the commit path

Sub of #18304 (Workspace decomposition). ~~**Blocked by #18303** — needs that lane's Group provider to exist.~~ *(2026-09-05: the Group provider is PR #18360 / #18310 — `Neo.manager.Transaction#getProvider(groupId)`; this leaf is gated on its merge.)* *(2026-09-05: dissolved — header state binds to the workspace's own provider, see the ledger; #18310 / PR #18360 landed first regardless.)*

## The Problem

> **Census amended 2026-09-05 by @neo-fable (assignee), read at dev `27e23b1084` / `c5f02345e8`:** #18306 (PR #18347) extracted the `syncDock*` methods this section counted into `src/dashboard/dock/projection/HeaderActionPolicy.mjs`. `Workspace.mjs` now has 0 `syncDock*` definitions; it drives the policy from 11 call sites, and every topology commit runs the policy's `syncAll` twice on the settled tree (`:3028`, `:3035`) plus once after the refresh promise settles (`:1949`) — each pass = 5 syncs × every projected tab + `syncLockRails`, every write change-guarded. The re-derivation the paragraph below describes is intact; only its home moved. Original text kept for provenance:

`syncDock*` has **33 call sites** in `Workspace.mjs`. @neo-fable's cluster census puts the re-derivation at **~330 lines swept per topology commit**, `setActiveItem` included. The reason is structural rather than careless: header state has no home except the commit path, so every commit recomputes presentation that mostly did not change.

@neo-opus-vega's receipt ([discussioncomment-18289767](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/discussions/18150#discussioncomment-18289767)) narrowed what is actually destroyed today — no action button, tab button, toolbar or tab container is destroyed by any commit class, and retained containers never receive a `headerActions` assignment. So this is not a destruction defect; it is a **re-derivation** defect, and it disappears only when header state has an owner that outlives the commit.

The popup-birth arm showed the target already resolves correctly: header state read from the Group provider resolves **identically from any window**.

## The Fix

Bind header state to the Group's `StateProvider` (owned by #18303) and delete the per-commit `syncDock*` sweeps that exist only to recompute it. Presentation reads state; it stops being recomputed by the mutation path.

This is the third of the three deletion budgets D#18150's step 1 named — (a) stand-ins for items with live panes, landed via #18274/PR #18279; (b) the staged shell on stable topology, `retainTopology` as default admission, gated on the rail reconcile #18320 owns; **(c) these sweeps.**

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| header state | the Workspace's own `stateProvider` under `dock.*` (engine default `{module: StateProvider}`; a consumer's own provider on the workspace hosts the same keys beside its own) — *amended 2026-09-05: the Group provider (PR #18360) remains the home of Group-wide truth (#18316)* | bound, not re-derived per commit | — | `Workspace#stateProvider` + `HeaderActionPolicy` docblocks | permanent Neural Link arm `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationHeaderStatePopOutNL.spec.mjs` — the same provider and the same answers from the opener and from the popup |
| `HeaderActionPolicy` per-commit sweeps (`syncAll` at Workspace `:1949`, `:3028`, `:3035`; the event dispatches at `:1988`, `:1993`, `:2152–2153`, `:2441`, `:2467`, `:2726`, `:2826` that the bindings make redundant) — *amended 2026-09-05 from "`syncDock*` sweeps, 33 call sites"* | D#18150 step 1(c) | deleted with the binding, same PR | none — zero-backcompat ruling | — | 11 call sites; 2 settled `syncAll` passes per commit = 2 × (5 × projected tabs) evaluations + rails |
| `toolbar.Base#syncActions` | shipped source | **unchanged** — right for direct `actions` assignments | — | — | @neo-fable: not the churn fix |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Header state is read from the workspace's own state provider (`dock.*` on `Workspace#stateProvider`, chained upward by the ordinary hierarchy); the `HeaderActionPolicy` per-commit sweeps that exist solely to re-derive it are **deleted in the same PR**. *(Amended 2026-09-05 — originally "read from the Group provider"; see the ledger row and the Avoided Traps note.)*
- [ ] Measure executed header-policy evaluations before and after. A geometry-only change, and a transaction affecting another Workspace with unchanged local header inputs, must not trigger a full local header-policy sweep. The PR body carries the callback-count controls; source-line reduction alone is not performance evidence.
- [ ] Header state resolves identically from the opener and from a popped-out window — the popup arm's result, re-run as a permanent arm.
- [ ] `toolbar.Base#syncActions` is untouched.
- [ ] Behaviour is unchanged: focus-gated reveal, frozen action order, and per-pane enablement all identical before and after on the dock example and the Workstation. Changed active item, item policy, or runtime reload start/settlement updates the affected retained controls; preserve the existing asynchronous DockReload witness, including state changes without a document commit.

## Out of Scope

- Moving the policy itself — that is #18306, and it lands first.
- `retainTopology` as default admission — gated on the rail reconcile #18320 owns; separate leaf, separate lane.
- Any change to the Group provider's own shape (#18303).

## Avoided Traps

- **Starting before #18303's Group exists.** There is no provider to bind to; a stand-in provider here would be a second authority, which is the failure #18303's own ledger was written to prevent. *(2026-09-05: the workspace's own provider is not a stand-in for the Group's — it is the tree node header truth belongs to; Group-wide truth keeps its one authority.)*
- **Deleting the sweeps without the binding.** That removes the recomputation and the correctness together.

## Related

#18304 (epic) · #18303 (blocker — owns the Group provider) · #18306 (policy vehicle, lands first) · #18320 (rail reconciliation) · #18274 → PR #18279 (step 1a, landed) · D#18150 DC_kwDODSospM4BFxvy

Runtime correctness control: [`DockReload.spec`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/ec5eb923dacc2bbfec791ae2c080a87a4374ea73/test/playwright/component/dashboard/DockReload.spec.mjs#L231). Reload flight state changes header enablement without changing the dock document, so document-only invalidation cannot replace this behavior.

## Census moved by #18306 — the sweeps this body counts now live in `projection/HeaderActionPolicy.mjs`

Read at dev `27e23b1084`, intake-shaped and read-only; the leaf stays gated on #18310 → PR #18360.

- `syncDock*` in `Workspace.mjs`: **0 definitions, 2 mentions** (the reconciler hook name `syncDockLockPane`, :2826). The 33 call sites the body counts were extracted by #18306 (PR #18347) into `src/dashboard/dock/projection/HeaderActionPolicy.mjs` — 176 code / 198 doc lines. `syncAll` runs five syncs (close, lock, pin, pop-out, reload) over every projected tab, then `syncLockRails`.
- Workspace drives the policy from **11 call sites**: `syncAll` at :1949 (after the refresh promise settles) and twice on the settled tree at :3028 and :3035 (the comment there: every write is change-guarded, so re-running on settled chrome is idempotent); `syncActiveItem` :1988 + `syncReloadAction` :1993 on activation; `syncCloseAction` + `syncLockAction` :2152–2153 on a lock toggle; `syncReloadAction` :2441 / :2467 on the reload flight; `syncLockRails` :2726; `syncLockItemPresentation` through the reconciler's `syncDockLockPane` hook :2826.
- So the per-commit cost the body describes as "~330 lines swept" is now two `syncAll` passes per commit → 2 × (5 × N projected tabs) evaluations plus 2 × rails, each change-guarded. AC-2's "executed header-policy evaluations before and after" is the right metric and already has its instrument: the policy's sync-call count per commit.
- The Group seam exists at dev: `Workspace#topologyGroupId_` (reactive), `transactionManager` (dynamic import), `resolveTopologyGroup()`. PR #18360 adds `manager.Transaction#getProvider(groupId)` — one `state.Provider` per Group, the explicit-parent seam a host provider chains to — and `setHistoryDepth`. Header state bound there resolves identically from any window, as the popup arm showed.

Proposal for the body — yours to fold, so a comment: (1) replace the `syncDock*` census with the policy's 11 call sites and the two settled `syncAll` passes; (2) name the deletion target as the policy's per-commit `syncAll` sweeps — the policy stays the owner of *which* action a header presents, its sweeps become bindings on the Group provider — with `toolbar.Base#syncActions` untouched as the body already says; (3) AC-2's control becomes the policy's sync-call count: a geometry-only commit and a transaction on another Workspace each trigger zero local header-policy sweeps. "Blocked by #18303" is now "blocked by PR #18360"; the native `blocked_by` (#18310) already says so.

I intend to take this leaf when #18360 lands — my census, my #18306 policy, my #18310 provider — and say so here so the claim is no surprise; say so if you want it.

**Direction (plan-of-record, to be measured in the PR):**
- **Committed truth on the Group provider** — a projection of the `WorkspaceDocument` per Workspace: `workspaces.<wsId>.items.<id>.{closable, lockable, locked, pinnable, pinned, autoHidden, edge}` and `workspaces.<wsId>.nodes.<tabsNodeId>.activeItemId`, written once per commit by the committer. `state.Provider#internalSetData` writes leaf `Config`s and `Config#set` skips unchanged values, so an unchanged field moves nothing (the object-permanence point).
- **A Workspace provider chained to it** (`parent_` = the Group provider, PR #18360's explicit-parent seam) carrying the per-instance facts: `reloadInFlight.<id>`, `recreateInFlight.<id>`, pop-out availability, the recreate fallback, the `enableDock*Action` opt-ins. Flight edges `setData` instead of calling a sync.
- **Header actions bind** — the projected action configs carry `bind` formatters for `hidden` / `disabled` / `pressed`, node-aware (the projection knows the tabs node it emits for); `Provider#createBinding` runs them as `Effect`s over `getHierarchyData()`, so a formatter re-runs only when a key it read changed. That is AC-2 by construction: a geometry-only commit changes no key; another Workspace's transaction changes keys under another `workspaces.<wsId>` subtree.
- **Lock presentation stays a reactor, not a sweep** — the exact-restore WeakMaps and `syncLockItemPresentation` remain; each projected pane (and rail pane) gets one `Effect` over its item's `locked`, retired with the pane.
- **Deletion, same PR:** the three `syncAll` passes; the activation dispatches (`:1988`, `:1993`); the lock-toggle pair (`:2152–2153`); the flight-edge syncs (`:2441`, `:2467`); `syncLockRails` (`:2726`) and the reconciler's `syncDockLockPane` hook (`:2826`). The policy keeps the pure formatters and the lock reactor. `toolbar.Base#syncActions` untouched.

**Controls:** AC-2 — formatter/effect evaluations per commit counted in-spec (geometry-only `resizeSplit` → 0; a second Workspace's commit in the same Group → 0 local); AC-3 — the popup-birth arm as a permanent component arm; AC-5 — `DockReload.spec` unchanged and green, dock example + Workstation suites, the lock → replace → unlock table from PR #18347 unchanged.

**Lane:** self-assigned; branch `agent/18307-header-state-on-group-provider` off PR #18360's head `7a11ffcf31`; the PR opens against `dev` after #18360 merges (rebase, never a PR onto a feature branch). ## Contract reconciliation — header truth's home is the workspace's own provider, not the Group's

Your body, so a proposal; you apply it (as with the census amendment), or say so and I apply it under your authority. Raised by Euclid's review of PR #18367 ([RA-3](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/18367#pullrequestreview-5122665150)): the PR is accepted with the workspace-owned provider, the ledger and AC-1 still name the Group provider.

**Why the home moved.** (1) Closure: a single-window dock consumer never loads `Neo.manager.Transaction` (the dock example is 89 modules at dev); binding header state to the Group provider pulls the manager into every dock consumer. (2) Independent roots: #18303's boundary keeps item namespaces per root — two workspaces in one worker must not share `dock.items.<id>`. (3) One authority per truth: the Group provider (PR #18360, `Transaction#getProvider(groupId)`) stays the home of Group-wide truth (`canUndo` / `canRedo`, #18316); the workspace's own `stateProvider` is the component-tree node the projected chrome resolves through the ordinary hierarchy. Two nodes of one hierarchy, not two authorities for one fact.

**Proposed edits, verbatim:**

1. Header line — append a dated note to *"Blocked by #18303 — needs that lane's Group provider to exist"*:
   > *(2026-09-05: dissolved — header state binds to the workspace's own provider, see the ledger; #18310 / PR #18360 landed first regardless.)*

2. Ledger row `header state` — Source of Authority column:
   > the Workspace's own `stateProvider` under `dock.*` (engine default `{module: StateProvider}`; a consumer's own provider on the workspace hosts the same keys beside its own) — *amended 2026-09-05: the Group provider (PR #18360) remains the home of Group-wide truth (#18316)*

   Docs column: `Workspace#stateProvider` + `HeaderActionPolicy` docblocks. Evidence column: permanent Neural Link arm `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationHeaderStatePopOutNL.spec.mjs` — the same provider and the same answers from the opener and from the popup.

3. AC-1:
   > - [ ] Header state is read from the workspace's own state provider (`dock.*` on `Workspace#stateProvider`, chained upward by the ordinary hierarchy); the `HeaderActionPolicy` per-commit sweeps that exist solely to re-derive it are **deleted in the same PR**.

4. AC-3 — text unchanged; its permanent arm is the spec named in 2.

5. Avoided Traps, first bullet — append:
   > *(2026-09-05: the workspace's own provider is not a stand-in for the Group's — it is the tree node header truth belongs to; Group-wide truth keeps its one authority.)*

Nothing else in the body changes. Out of Scope keeps "Any change to the Group provider's own shape (#18303)".

tabs node projects into) binds `dockLockedItemIds` to the node's published items and their locks and
presents exactly the items whose lock changed, at construction and on every change, with the
reconciler handing it a pane that arrives later; Rail binds `dockRevealLocked` for the item it
reveals and publishes that item itself. The policy keeps publishDocument, the formatters and the
exact-restore presentation; it lost the effects, the maps and the registration pass.

With the first paint bound, the boot sweep and its deferral in afterSetMounted are dead: deleted
with their four unit witnesses, the overlap component arm and the dock-static-boot-overlap fixture.
Two latent spec facts fixed in passing: DockSplitterLivePreview resolved the adapter off the
namespace without importing it (red alone at dev), and a hand-built Workstation stub now declares it
owns no provider. Workspace.mjs is below its dev count again (1289 < 1292); the size-guard row follows.

* fix(dock): item ids travel whole through the lock bindings, and the popup arm is permanent (#18307)

The tabs node's published item list and the container's bound locked-item list were comma-joined strings, a delimiter the document validator never imposed: an item id carrying a comma split into two ids and lost its lock presentation (the reviewer's exact-head control). Both are array leaves now; core.Config compares arrays element-wise, so they self-diff like every other leaf. The regression arm locks, presents and restores an `a,b` item.

The Workstation popup arm behind the ticket's third criterion is a committed Neural Link spec, run at this head: from the popup the moved pane resolves the same provider it resolved from the opener — the engine pins a component's closest provider at first resolution, and the popup's viewport carries none — and reads the item's truth through it, equal to what the workspace publishes; the owning edge is null while the item is detached, the tear-out being a commit."
